meta.scope: Uruguay batch 5 — Social security (BPS), construction activity, tourism/hospitality employment signals, and final social-protection anchors. Closing expansion pass.

candidates.title: Banco de Previsión Social (BPS) — social-security coverage and finances
candidates.description: Main social-security institution covering pensions, family allowances, unemployment benefits, sickness benefits and other social transfers. Major fiscal and social-protection actor.
candidates.notes: Central social-protection node. 2025 benefit outlays on the order of USD 8+ bn, dominated by pensions. Continuously cited in fiscal, labour and social-policy analysis; cotizante counts are a key formal-employment indicator.

candidates.title: Jubilaciones y pensiones (BPS)
candidates.description: Pension and retirement benefit statistics administered by BPS. Largest single component of social-security expenditure.
candidates.notes: Dominant BPS expenditure line. Hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries; major structural claim on public resources.

candidates.title: Actividad de la construcción / Construction activity
candidates.description: Statistics of construction activity, employment and related permits. Cyclically sensitive sector tracked via employment, permits and investment indicators.
candidates.notes: Important short-term activity and employment sector. BPS cotizante counts in construction are a high-frequency formal-employment signal; unemployment benefits often concentrate in this sector in downturns.

candidates.title: Turismo y hotelería / Tourism & hospitality
candidates.description: Tourism and hospitality activity and employment statistics. Important services-export and seasonal employment sector, especially in coastal departments.
candidates.notes: Services-side complement to the agro-export economy. Hospitality employment is a useful high-frequency signal of tourism and domestic consumption dynamics.

candidates.title: FONASA / Seguro Nacional de Salud
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministerio de Salud Pública / MEF
candidates.description: National health-insurance scheme financing coverage through mutualistas and the public provider (ASSE). Major component of the social-security and health-financing system.
candidates.notes: Central health-financing mechanism. Linked to BPS contributions and to the public health budget; methodological parameters (e.g. CPE) are periodically reviewed.

candidates.title: ASSE — Administración de los Servicios de Salud del Estado
candidates.description: Public health-service provider. Complements the mutualista sector within the national health system.
candidates.notes: Public provider side of the dual health system. Linked to FONASA financing and to the health functional budget.

candidates.title: Departamento de Flores — low-poverty interior contrast
candidates.description: Small interior department with among the lowest poverty and inequality incidence.
candidates.notes: Completes the low-poverty set. Useful as a small-department contrast to the high-poverty border departments.

candidates.title: Departamento de Salto — northern interior
candidates.description: Northern interior department with elevated inequality and intermediate-to-higher poverty relative to the southern core.
candidates.notes: Frequently appears among the higher-inequality departments. Completes the northern departmental set.

candidates.title: Asignaciones familiares y transferencias (BPS)
candidates.description: Family allowances and related cash-transfer programmes administered by BPS. Important social-protection instrument for households with children.
candidates.notes: Key non-pension social-transfer line. Complements the pension system within the BPS benefit structure.

candidates.title: Cotizantes BPS / Formal employment contributors
candidates.description: Count of formal workers contributing to BPS. High-frequency formal-employment indicator complementary to the ECH labour series.
candidates.notes: Useful formal-employment signal. Sectoral breakdowns (construction, hospitality, industry, agro, etc.) provide high-frequency insight into formal job dynamics.

proposed_edges.basis: Pensions are the largest single BPS expenditure line.
Family allowances are a core BPS social-transfer programme.
Cotizante counts are a primary administrative product of BPS.
FONASA is administered within the broader social-security and contribution system managed by BPS.
Construction employment is tracked via BPS cotizante counts among other sources.
Hospitality employment is a useful high-frequency signal drawn from BPS sectoral cotizante data.
ASSE is a major public provider financed in part through the FONASA system.
